jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a strategic leadership role responsible for defining and advancing SE Health’s enterprise architecture vision. This position establishes architecture discipline as a cornerstone of SE Health’s modernization strategy by aligning technology capabilities with business priorities, enabling digital transformation, and ensuring successful integration of critical platforms such as the digital patient record, people/finance/payroll systems, contact center, service management, and others.

The Director leads enterprise-wide architecture decisions that drive agility, scalability, security, and measurable business outcomes. This includes building and maturing the Enterprise Architecture function, establishing an Architecture Review Board, and delivering a three-year technology roadmap that incorporates strategic platforms, cloud strategy, data and analytics capabilities, integration architecture, and security and compliance posture. The Director ensures successful architecture and integration of platforms such as Alayacare and Workday, while driving adoption of best practices, standards, and governance across technology domains. By translating business objectives into coherent, secure, and sustainable technology designs, the Director plays a critical role in spearheading a digital transformation that enhances the experience of patients, families, employees, and clients, supporting SE Health’s mission of exceptional home and community care.

Primary Accountabilities

Enterprise Architecture Strategy and Governance

Develop and execute an enterprise architecture strategy and multi-year roadmap that enables modernization, interoperability, and alignment with organizational goals, including maximizing value from core enterprise platforms (e.g., Alayacare, Workday).
Establish and lead enterprise architecture governance processes (e.g., an Architecture Review Board or Enterprise Architecture Council) to define standards, manage technical debt, and inform major technology and investment decisions.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the CDO, CIO, CTO, and senior leadership, translating business priorities into sustainable, secure, enterprise-wide technology designs.
Assess and improve enterprise architecture maturity, documenting improvements and outcomes aligned to business KPIs and informing continuous evolution of architecture practices.
Drive mission-critical enterprise architecture and data modernization projects, providing strategic oversight and ensuring integration, scalability, and compliance across platforms and business functions.

Technology, Cloud and Systems Integration Architecture

Lead the architecture, integration, and modernization of core enterprise platforms, including Alayacare, Workday, Procura, ERP, CRM, HRIS, Finance, and scheduling systems, to enable a cohesive and interoperable ecosystem across business and clinical operations.
Define and oversee enterprise reference architectures, integration and data standards, patterns, and roadmaps that promote modernization, automation, analytics enablement, and business process optimization.
Lead modernization efforts to rationalize applications, reduce technical debt, and migrate or retire legacy platforms using a cloud-smart, scalable approach.
Oversee enterprise solution architecture across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments to ensure performance, resilience, security, and cost-efficiency, including multi-cloud strategy across AWS and Azure.
Guide adoption of architectural best practices across security, operational excellence, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization domains.
Review and evaluate solution designs and technology proposals, providing direction and recommendations through architecture governance forums.
Analyze enterprise technology and data architecture requirements to support new applications, system scalability, and platform integrations.

Leadership, People and Continuous Improvement

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing enterprise architecture team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and excellence.
Drive continuous improvement and EA maturity by introducing modern frameworks, methodologies, and tooling (e.g., TOGAF, HOPEX) to enhance consistency, documentation, and solution quality.
Embed security and privacy by design across architecture practices, ensuring adherence to cybersecurity, privacy, and healthcare compliance requirements.
Build strong partnerships with Digital, Security, and Business leaders to influence technology strategy, support demand intake, and ensure alignment of solutions to business needs.
Champion digital transformation and innovation by evaluating emerging technologies (e.g., mobile, IoT, telehealth, AI) and recommending their adoption where they advance SE Health’s mission and services.

Data and Analytics Architecture

Define enterprise data architecture strategies, standards, and models that enable analytics, AI, and data-driven decision-making across the organization.
Partner with Data & Analytics teams to design and evolve data platforms (e.g., data lake/warehouse) to support enterprise information management, governance, reporting, and advanced analytics.
Provide leadership, guidance, and mentoring to data architecture and solution design teams on data and integration best practices.
Collaborate with data science and analytics teams to support AI-enabled insights, intelligent automation, and emerging technologies that drive value for clinical and business functions.

AI, Automation & Intelligent Systems

Lead integration of AI-driven insights and intelligent automation into enterprise applications and workflows.
Partner with data science teams to enable machine learning, predictive analytics, and data-driven optimization across clinical and business functions.
Evaluate emerging AI/automation technologies and define architectural guardrails for safe, ethical, and scalable adoption.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field. Experience with EA frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, ArchiMate, or similar) is preferred.
12+ years of experience in enterprise/solution architecture, including leading modernization and large-scale integration initiatives in complex environments.
5+ years of leadership experience managing architecture teams, building high-performing technical talent, and advancing enterprise architecture maturity.
Strong expertise across enterprise, application, data, and technology architecture, with hands-on experience in cloud and integration architectures (AWS/Azure, APIs, microservices, event-driven design).
Experience leading architecture for major SaaS platforms (e.g., CRM, ERP, HR systems); Alayacare and/or Workday strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of data architecture, governance, and analytics enablement; experience with AI/ML-enabled solutions is an asset.
Knowledge of security, privacy, and compliance considerations for enterprise platforms and data.
Experience in healthcare or other highly regulated industries is an asset.
Exceptional communication, consulting, and stakeholder engagement skills, with proven ability to influence executives and simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.

Why join SE Health?

Competitive Total Rewards So much more than a paycheque! Enjoy comprehensive benefits, pension, flexible pay options, car-loan support, housing solutions and exclusive staff perks.
Flexibility & Belonging Thrive with hybrid work, flexible scheduling and a supportive, inclusive culture that puts people first.
Purpose & Impact Join a national social enterprise where your voice matters. Every role helps advance health, spark innovation and strengthen communities across Canada.
Growth That Meets Your Ambition Access tuition support, training and meaningful career pathways across a growing, future-focused organization.

SE Health is a not-for-profit social enterprise advancing health with heart. With 115+ years of impact, we bring hope, happiness and exceptional care to people and communities across Canada. We lead with empathy, dignity and purpose while building a future where everyone can realize their full health and well-being potential. À propos du poste

McKesson
est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données
stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

Ce que vous ferez

Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.
Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.
Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.
Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.
Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.
Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.
Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.
Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Exigences de base

Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.
Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.
Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.
Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.
Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.
Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées

Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.
Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.

Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.

Join CoolIT, an Ecolab Company, a global leader in Direct Liquid Cooling technology for data centers, supercomputers, and high-performance computing environments.

CoolIT is seeking a Director of Enterprise Architecture
to provide the architectural vision and strategic technology leadership needed to support our future growth. You will partner with senior business and technology leaders to translate strategic priorities into integrated process, data, and technology strategies, target-state architectures, and multi-year roadmaps.

This is a forward-looking, director-level position focused on shaping long-term architecture decisions rather than providing day-to-day operational support. You will guide enterprise resource planning modernization, including NetSuite and the broader enterprise application landscape, while establishing

technology direction for Manufacturing and the Integrated Supply Chain in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial capabilities. You will also evaluate emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, software-as-a-service solutions, automation, Industrial Internet of Things, and cloud and edge technologies, to determine how they can support the future of work and deliver measurable business value.

What You Will Do

Partner with Enterprise Business Engagement Managers and Business Relationship Managers to translate business priorities into integrated process, data, and technology strategies, capability roadmaps, and investment priorities.
Develop and maintain three-to-five-year technology roadmaps for enterprise resource planning, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and other key enterprise functions.
Establish the enterprise resource planning modernization strategy for NetSuite evolution, capability optimization, application simplification, and future-state architecture.
Define technology strategies and target-state architectures for Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Digital Plant capabilities in alignment with Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial priorities.
Collaborate with Solution Architects and Platform Architects to develop reference, target-state, and transition architectures spanning business processes, technology platforms, data, integration, security, and infrastructure.
Lead application rationalization and modernization initiatives that reduce technical debt, duplication, unnecessary customization, and complexity across the enterprise application landscape.
Evaluate and guide the strategic adoption of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, automation, data and analytics, Industrial Internet of Things, software-as-a-service solutions, and cloud and edge technologies.
Participate in future-of-work discussions and identify emerging technology opportunities that can improve productivity, resilience, scalability, and sustainability.
Oversee architecture governance and strategic technology decisions while ensuring alignment with established enterprise architecture principles, frameworks, and standards.
Advise and influence senior business and technology leaders by connecting business strategy, architectural direction, technology investment, and execution.

This is a director-level position focused primarily on architectural vision, future growth, emerging technologies, and long-term strategic roadmaps rather than day-to-day operational support.

Experience developing enterprise resource planning strategies and leading modernization initiatives, ideally involving NetSuite and exposure to large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms.
Experience with Supply Chain and Manufacturing capabilities and cross-functional Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial processes and platforms.
Knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks, principles, and practices across business processes, technology platforms, data, integration, cybersecurity, and infrastructure.
Experience developing business capability models, reference architectures, target-state architectures, and transition roadmaps.
Experience applying data, integration, cloud and edge, artificial intelligence, and cybersecurity architecture principles.
Experience influencing senior business and technology leaders and guiding strategic technology decisions across organizational boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading a major enterprise resource planning modernization or transformation program involving NetSuite, SAP, Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, or Microsoft Dynamics 365.
Enterprise architecture design experience across Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Finance, Human Resources, and Commercial functions.
Experience with Smart Manufacturing, Digital Plant, and Industrial Internet of Things technologies.
Knowledge of process and discrete manufacturing environments, including batch manufacturing, formulation management, lot traceability, quality, product stewardship, and regulatory compliance.
Practical experience applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, or intelligent automation to enterprise business processes.
Experience evaluating and implementing software-as-a-service platforms and emerging enterprise technologies.

Demonstrated ability to connect strategy and execution, influence across organizational boundaries, and advise senior leaders as a trusted partner.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Contracting and Financial Operations, the Director, Distribution, Contracting & Compensation Operations is responsible for leading day-to-day operations with a strong focus on operational performance, data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement and modernization across the broader Contracting and Compensation department. The role is accountable for translating operational insights into practical improvements that strengthen efficiency, capacity, service, quality and the employee, customer and advisor experience.

The Director works closely with the Director, Strategic Initiatives and broader strategic initiatives team, providing operational expertise and partnership on larger transformation priorities, while maintaining primary accountability for operational execution, continuous improvement and modernization within the business.

We are looking for a data-driven leader with a strong operations and continuous improvement mindset who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You actively use operational statistics to understand volumes, backlog, productivity, capacity, service levels and quality—connecting trends to root causes, measuring results and using those insights to simplify processes, improve performance and identify opportunities for automation and modernization. You see the bigger picture, solve problems quickly and scale practical improvements while balancing operational outcomes with risk, financial discipline and exceptional employee, customer and advisor experiences.

The Director will oversee a team of leaders, supporting the Contracts & Compensation operations team that resides in three locations across Canada (Toronto, London & Winnipeg).. As a member of the Contracting & Financial Operations senior leadership team, you will shape shared priorities, bring an operational lens to broader strategic initiatives, champion continuous improvement and modernization, and represent the team in senior-level operational forums.

Data-driven analytical and problem-solving skills: use operational statistics, dashboards and root-cause analysis to drive measurable improvements in productivity, quality and service.
Strong communication and collaboration skills to influence peers and stakeholders and represent the team in external operations meetings with senior leadership.
End-to-end process knowledge, financial acumen and sound judgement in balancing capacity, costs, service and enterprise risk controls.

Strategic thinking and a transformation mindset, with experience in lean process improvement, strategic projects and leading cross-functional initiatives through execution and adoption.

Overview

Reporting to the Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and operating under the oversight of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Chief Actuary is a senior leader accountable for the Corporation’s claims & premiums forecasting, rate setting, policy liability valuation, investments, asset-liability management, stress testing capital, and reinsurance.

The Chief Actuary represents the Corporation before the Public Utilities Board (PUB) during the annual General Rate Application (GRA), providing actuarial expertise and expert testimony. The role has oversight from the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) also serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Executive Management team, leveraging actuarial analysis and statistical research to support key business decisions and organizational change. In addition, the Chief Actuary contributes to governance through participation on committees overseeing claims, investments, and enterprise risk management.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Transformation:
Lead the development of strategies for pricing and capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments.
Provide expert advice and guidance on the Corporation’s financial forecasting, rate setting, valuation of policy liabilities, investments, asset and liability management, stress testing of capital and reinsurance.
Oversee the design, implementation, and reporting of the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management strategy.
Develop and implement processes to ensure a current understanding of new and emerging trends, practices and solutions.
Develop and implement processes and practices to evaluate MPI’s ability to meet needs and address future conditions or issues.
Create strategies to position the Corporation in the future by anticipating and acting on trends.
Translate the strategic plans into operational and business plans for pricing, capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments and set operational objectives to all employees.

Operational & Performance Leadership:
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Basic line of business and provide professional opinion on the appropriateness of these rates to the PUB.
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Extension line of business.
Determine actuarially sound rates for Commercial lines and collaborate with key stakeholders to incorporate strategic, operational, and competitive requirements into the proposed rates.
Ensure the effective design, maintenance, controls, and output of key pricing models.
Testify at the PUB rate hearings on behalf of the Corporation.
Perform quarterly reviews of the Corporation’s policy liabilities for all lines of business.
Work collaboratively with the External Appointed Actuary to obtain an external signed actuarial opinion on the policy liability reviews.
Monitor claims reporting and reserving guidelines, in collaboration with key internal stakeholders.
Contribute to the forecasting process by providing actuarial forecasts by line of business and include premiums, claims costs, expenses, and investment income.
Lead the design, maintenance, and on-going enhancement of the Corporation’s financial forecasting model.
Provide financial modelling and scenario analysis for strategic decisions from the Executive and the Board of Directors.
Lead the design, maintenance, and output of the stochastic models used to simulate the behaviour of claims, interest rates, investment returns, and other economic variables.
Perform Financial Condition Testing for each line of business to stress test the capital for satisfactory financial condition and provide a signed actuarial opinion.
Oversee the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management program to meet the programs’ objectives.
Perform commutation analysis for the Corporation’s reinsurance contracts and participate in the negotiation of reinsurance contracts.
Monitor investment performance and report investment performance to the Investment Committee of the Board of Directors.

Organizational & People Leadership:
Establish and maintain an effective organizational structure that supports the strategic delivery of services, ensuring alignment with corporate priorities and operational excellence.
Foster a unified and high-performing leadership team that is collaborative, future-focused, and committed to advancing the Corporation’s mission through continuous service improvement and innovation.
Champion a culture of accountability, inclusion, and excellence, where diverse perspectives are valued, calculated risks are embraced, and employees are empowered to deliver exceptional service and contribute meaningfully to the Corporation’s success.

Education:
Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries (FCIA) and Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS).
The CFA designation and/or strong investment knowledge is considered as an asset.

Experience:
Ten (10) years of senior leadership experience at the Director or Senior Director level, including five (5) years in a senior actuarial leadership capacity within the property and casualty insurance industry, with accountability for strategic rate setting, reserving, enterprise risk management, and actuarial governance.

Technical Knowledge and Skills:
Exceptional leadership skills with a proven ability to form, lead and develop high performing teams, and demonstrate successes in leading change.
Superior negotiation skills along with excellent interpersonal skills and proven success in public speaking and formal presentations.
Proven experience effectively and critically assessing different product and coverage scenarios and determining creative solutions that meet customers’ needs while demonstrating clear understanding of root cause, impacts and consequences of decisions on both customers and the corporation.
Strong organizational skills along with the ability to plan and manage multiple complex projects and tasks simultaneously will contribute to success in this role.
Capable of positively engaging executive management, the Board of Directors as well as influential external stakeholders (e.g. Government of Manitoba, strategic business partners, interest groups with diverging interests) and operate with the highest level of integrity and business ethics.

Head of Revenue - Full-time, Remote

Application Deadline: November 29th, 2026 @ 11:59pm EST

Build the revenue engine that takes BeMo to the next stage of growth.

Why BeMo?

At BeMo, our mission is rooted in the belief that education is a universal right, not a privilege. We help students pursue highly competitive professional programs through admissions consulting, test preparation, and technology-enabled services. Our team is remote, fast-moving, data-driven, and focused on measurable student and business outcomes.

The Role:

We are looking for a commercially rigorous Head of Revenue to own the full revenue system across demand generation, sales, expansion, lifecycle revenue, and revenue operations. This is not a traditional sales-leadership role. Your job is to identify the biggest constraint on profitable growth, quantify the opportunity, prioritize the highest-leverage initiatives, and lead cross-functional execution.

You will be accountable for increasing cash and revenue while protecting the quality and economics of growth. You will work directly with the CEO and lead the revenue organization toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory.

What You Will Own:

Company-wide revenue growth across marketing, sales, direct/self-serve revenue, upsells, cross-sells, downsells, saves, referrals, and reactivation.
Demand generation economics, including qualified lead volume, cost per qualified request, CAC, ROI/ROAS, and channel-level growth efficiency.
Sales performance, including completed consultations, revenue per completed call, conversion rate, AOV, show efficiency, response speed, and forecasting accuracy.
Pricing, packaging, offers, promotions, and lifecycle monetization designed to increase customer value without relying on short-term pull-forward tactics.
Revenue operations: attribution, dashboards, lead tracking, funnel measurement, forecasting, QA, and reliable experiment measurement.
A disciplined testing program across acquisition, landing pages, sales, follow-up, email/SMS/direct mail, offers, and expansion revenue.
Cross-functional prioritization: decide where the next dollar and the next hour of team capacity create the highest expected incremental value.
Revenue leadership systems that reduce dependence on any single individual and create repeatable, scalable execution.

How Success Will Be Measured:

The role carries a significant performance-based component aligned with the same outcomes the role controls. Performance is evaluated across three dimensions:
Cash growth: durable improvement in actual cash received.
Demand generation: growth in qualified demand and channel economics, not traffic or lead volume in isolation.
Strategic execution: completion and quality of the systems, experiments, reporting, automation, and longer-term initiatives required to compound revenue growth.

These outcomes are also subject to a company growth-driver score that prevents one strong metric from masking deterioration elsewhere in the revenue system. The objective is sustainable progress toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory, not local optimization of one department.

What You Will Do:

Diagnose the revenue funnel and identify the highest-value constraint before prescribing solutions.
Build quarterly revenue plans with quantified assumptions, targets, owners, timelines, and expected impact.
Lead the Sales Manager and coordinate tightly with marketing, operations, support, finance, and DevOps.
Set and monitor leading and lagging KPIs across acquisition, sales, and expansion revenue.
Design and review experiments with defined hypotheses, controls, success metrics, guardrails, and decision rules.
Improve the economics of paid and organic acquisition while maintaining sufficient qualified demand for the sales organization.
Increase revenue per lead and revenue per customer through better conversion, AOV, offers, upsells, cross-sells, and reactivation.
Build accurate forecasting, attribution, and executive reporting so decisions are based on trusted data.
Use AI and automation where they improve speed, conversion, decision quality, or operating leverage.
Develop leaders, delegate execution appropriately, and hold teams accountable for both results and quality.

We’d Love to Hear From You if You…

Have 7+ years of progressively senior revenue, growth, commercial, sales, or marketing leadership experience.
Can demonstrate material revenue growth you personally helped cause, with baseline, endpoint, time period, and measurable contribution.
Have owned more than one part of the revenue system - ideally demand generation plus sales, lifecycle/expansion, or RevOps.
Are highly quantitative and can translate funnel changes into incremental revenue, cash, CAC, and contribution economics.
Have managed leaders and teams rather than relying on personal heroics.
Can distinguish correlation from causation and are comfortable changing your view when the data contradicts your initial hypothesis.
Know how to prioritize aggressively and can explain what should not be done yet.
Have strong attention to detail, forecasting discipline, and operating cadence.
Are comfortable in a remote, high-accountability environment and can work across functions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Compensation & Location:

Remote role. Potential total annual compensation up to $300,000+ CAD, including competitive base compensation and a significant performance based bonus tied to cash growth, demand generation, strategic execution, and progress against the company's long term revenue growth plan. Final compensation will depend on experience and performance.

Our Hiring Process:

Our hiring process includes multiple steps. You will progress to each step if we believe there's a good match for both parties. The process includes a review of your application, a skills assessment test, a virtual OR phone interview, a face-to-face interview with select members of our team via video conference and lastly, reference calls.

How to Apply:

Simple. Click "Apply" and fill out the short application form.

We won’t be able to individually respond to all applicants, but if we feel that you’re a strong match, we will be in touch via email to proceed with your application. Thanks, and we look forward to hearing from you!

Client Success Managers own the commercial relationship, account health and renewals. Adoption Specialists drive radiologist and administrator enablement, including SmartAssist rollouts. The director runs both as one motion, with the Client Success Manager accountable for the account and the Adoption Specialist work planned against each account's goals.

As Jacobian's US customer base grows, this director will scale both teams to match. That means planning headcount ahead of demand, hiring and onboarding new team members, and building repeatable playbooks and coverage models so service quality holds as account and site volume increase. The role partners closely with Implementation, Support, Sales, Marketing, and Product teams. Drive growth through our existing customers by ensuring each one is live, engaged, and achieving measurable clinical and operational results, earning their renewal, expansion, and advocacy.

Operating model: Define US customer segmentation (high-touch, scaled, digital), the engagement model and coverage ratios for each tier, and the customer lifecycle from the go-live handoff through renewal.
Team leadership: Hire, onboard, coach, and retain Client Success Managers and Adoption Specialists. Define role profiles and career paths between the two roles, run a regular performance-management cadence, and plan headcount ahead of customer growth
Training and adoption: Lead new-customer training on Fluency for Imaging, from administrator onboarding through radiologist go-live. Run adoption programs for AI features such as SmartAssist, own speech recognition tuning and troubleshooting, and set utilization benchmarks by product
Customer health and risk: Build health scores in HubSpot from FFI usage, SmartAssist adoption, speech recognition performance, support trends, and sentiment. Set early-warning signals, and own how at-risk accounts are identified, escalated, and recovered
Value and retention: Lead executive business reviews that show customers the clinical and operational value they are getting. Own the US renewal calendar and forecast

Growth and advocacy: Partner with Sales on expansion opportunities and clean pre- and post-sale handoffs, and with Marketing on references and customer advocacy
Cross-team handoffs: Own the customer relationship across Implementation and Technical Support. Set exit criteria for the go-live handoff from Implementation, and coordinate with Technical Support on escalations and recurring issues so customers get one consistent experience
Scaled engagement: Serve smaller accounts efficiently through HubSpot-driven touchpoints, triggered playbooks, AI-assisted account preparation, and meeting capture
Voice of the customer: Bring structured customer feedback to Product, Clinical, and the executive team. Close the loop on adoption friction and feature requests, and represent customers in roadmap discussions
Financial accountability: Accountable for gross and net revenue retention, churn, and renewal and expansion targets for US accounts. Contributes to the Client Success budget and headcount plan with the VP, Client Success
Quality and compliance: Make sure customer feedback that may be a complaint is routed into Jacobian's complaint-handling process. Partner with Legal, Security, and Compliance on protecting customer data under HIPAA

Why SiftMed
SiftMed is an AI company in St. John’s, Newfoundland. Insurance carriers, independent medical examiners and legal teams use our platform to review medical records in claims. It finds the facts a case turns on, like pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps and causation evidence, across thousands of pages. Each finding links to its source page, and customers cut review time by 50 to 70 percent. We handle some of the most sensitive data there is, so security and privacy shape every product decision.

Revenue grew 10X in 2025. In July 2026 we closed a round led by Staircase Ventures, with the founders of Verafin, bringing our total funding to more than $10 million. We’re opening a new office and have more customer demand than people to meet it. Titles and comp are flexible for the right person. If you want your work to matter from your first week and want to help build a company that started in Newfoundland, we’d love to talk.

The role
You'll own the full customer lifecycle at SiftMed: pilots, onboarding, adoption, retention and expansion. You'll write the playbook for how we work with every customer, from strategic accounts to smaller ones, and make sure each one gets real value from SiftMed long after the contract is signed.

You'll report to our VP, Product and work closely with Sales, Product and Engineering. To start, you'll run pilots and onboarding yourself. As SiftMed grows, you'll build and lead a customer team to take on more of that work.

What you'll do

Pilots and onboarding
Design the playbook for how we manage every SiftMed customer, from first pilot to renewal
Run pilots during the sales cycle with Sales and Product, and manage strategic pilots end to end as program manager
Build and scale our onboarding process, and handle configuration for new customers

Adoption and retention
Design adoption, training and outreach plans for priority customers and smaller accounts
Define customer health scores from product usage and engagement, and flag at-risk accounts well ahead of renewal
Confirm new customers have fully replaced their old review process, and retrain accounts when key stakeholders change
Own how we announce new releases to customers, and use them to re-engage quiet accounts

Expansion and product
Find growth opportunities in existing accounts and run expansion plans with Sales and Product
Turn feedback across accounts into roadmap priorities, scope fixes for adoption blockers with Engineering, and tell customers what we built for them
Use AI to analyze usage data and customer feedback, and to draft customer communications

Who you are
You build a process, then run it yourself until someone else can.
You notice when an account goes quiet, and you act on it long before renewal.
You can turn scattered customer feedback into a clear priority for the product team.
You work well across Sales, Product and Engineering, and you get things done without needing to manage everyone involved.
You want to grow into leading a team.

This role probably isn't right for you if you want a team in place on day one.

What you bring
You use AI tools every day to work faster and better, and you can show us how. This is required for every role at SiftMed.
10+ years in customer success, account management or implementation for B2B software
Experience designing and running onboarding and adoption programs across a full book of customers
Experience running pilots or proofs of concept with enterprise customers during a sales cycle
Experience defining customer health metrics and using product usage data to manage retention
Experience working with Product and Engineering to turn customer feedback into product changes

Bonus points
Background in insurance, legal or healthcare software
Experience building or leading a customer success team
Experience with Salesforce or product analytics tools

If you don't match every item here, apply anyway.

Your first six months
First month: Learn the product in depth and meet our customers alongside Sales and Product
Within 3 months: Run your first pilot and onboard new customers using a playbook you've written
Within 4 months: Launch customer health scores across our full customer book
By 6 months: Own the customer lifecycle end to end, with an adoption and expansion plan for every priority account

Behind every medical file we review is a person waiting on a decision about their claim. We take that seriously. We don’t take ourselves too seriously. Everyone has a seat at the table, whatever their role. Your ideas shape what we build, and you’ll have the trust and autonomy to act on them.

Four times a year, the whole company heads out of the office for “Boil-Up.” In Newfoundland, a boil-up means stopping to boil the kettle over an open fire for tea and a bite to eat. Ours is a week of strategic planning and fun, where everyone helps set direction for the months ahead. Between Boil-Ups, you’ll find us on the pickleball court, laughing together and celebrating life's special occasions.

We offer flexible, hybrid work because we trust our people. You won’t need to ask twice to do school drop-off or get to a mid-day appointment. We serve a wide range of people, so we need a team with a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We welcome applicants from every background. Permanent Full Time

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Contracting and Financial Operations, the Director, Distribution, Contracting & Compensation Operations is responsible for leading day-to-day operations with a strong focus on operational performance, data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement and modernization across the broader Contracting and Compensation department. The role is accountable for translating operational insights into practical improvements that strengthen efficiency, capacity, service, quality and the employee, customer and advisor experience.

The Director works closely with the Director, Strategic Initiatives and broader strategic initiatives team, providing operational expertise and partnership on larger transformation priorities, while maintaining primary accountability for operational execution, continuous improvement and modernization within the business.

We are looking for a data-driven leader with a strong operations and continuous improvement mindset who thrives in a fast-paced environment. You actively use operational statistics to understand volumes, backlog, productivity, capacity, service levels and quality—connecting trends to root causes, measuring results and using those insights to simplify processes, improve performance and identify opportunities for automation and modernization. You see the bigger picture, solve problems quickly and scale practical improvements while balancing operational outcomes with risk, financial discipline and exceptional employee, customer and advisor experiences.

The Director will oversee a team of leaders, supporting the Contracts & Compensation operations team that resides in three locations across Canada (Toronto, London & Winnipeg).. As a member of the Contracting & Financial Operations senior leadership team, you will shape shared priorities, bring an operational lens to broader strategic initiatives, champion continuous improvement and modernization, and represent the team in senior-level operational forums.

What You Will Do

Coach, mentor and develop the Contracts & Compensation leadership team through people-centric leadership, positive influence and clear expectations; prioritize engagement and employee experience alongside operational results.
Manage performance using operational statistics, dashboards and trends. Monitor volumes, backlog, productivity, capacity, service levels and quality; investigate variances and root causes and implement plans to reduce redundancies, improve efficiency and simplify doing business. new_jobs.description:
Overview

Reporting to the Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and operating under the oversight of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Chief Actuary is a senior leader accountable for the Corporation’s claims & premiums forecasting, rate setting, policy liability valuation, investments, asset-liability management, stress testing capital, and reinsurance.

The Chief Actuary represents the Corporation before the Public Utilities Board (PUB) during the annual General Rate Application (GRA), providing actuarial expertise and expert testimony. The role has oversight from the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) also serves as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Executive Management team, leveraging actuarial analysis and statistical research to support key business decisions and organizational change. In addition, the Chief Actuary contributes to governance through participation on committees overseeing claims, investments, and enterprise risk management.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Transformation:
Lead the development of strategies for pricing and capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments.
Provide expert advice and guidance on the Corporation’s financial forecasting, rate setting, valuation of policy liabilities, investments, asset and liability management, stress testing of capital and reinsurance.
Oversee the design, implementation, and reporting of the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management strategy.
Develop and implement processes to ensure a current understanding of new and emerging trends, practices and solutions.
Develop and implement processes and practices to evaluate MPI’s ability to meet needs and address future conditions or issues.
Create strategies to position the Corporation in the future by anticipating and acting on trends.
Translate the strategic plans into operational and business plans for pricing, capital management, reserving, forecasting, reinsurance and investments and set operational objectives to all employees.

Operational & Performance Leadership:
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Basic line of business and provide professional opinion on the appropriateness of these rates to the PUB.
Determine actuarially sound rates for the Extension line of business.
Determine actuarially sound rates for Commercial lines and collaborate with key stakeholders to incorporate strategic, operational, and competitive requirements into the proposed rates.
Ensure the effective design, maintenance, controls, and output of key pricing models.
Testify at the PUB rate hearings on behalf of the Corporation.
Perform quarterly reviews of the Corporation’s policy liabilities for all lines of business.
Work collaboratively with the External Appointed Actuary to obtain an external signed actuarial opinion on the policy liability reviews.
Monitor claims reporting and reserving guidelines, in collaboration with key internal stakeholders.
Contribute to the forecasting process by providing actuarial forecasts by line of business and include premiums, claims costs, expenses, and investment income.
Lead the design, maintenance, and on-going enhancement of the Corporation’s financial forecasting model.
Provide financial modelling and scenario analysis for strategic decisions from the Executive and the Board of Directors.
Lead the design, maintenance, and output of the stochastic models used to simulate the behaviour of claims, interest rates, investment returns, and other economic variables.
Perform Financial Condition Testing for each line of business to stress test the capital for satisfactory financial condition and provide a signed actuarial opinion.
Oversee the Corporation’s Asset and Liability Management program to meet the programs’ objectives.
Perform commutation analysis for the Corporation’s reinsurance contracts and participate in the negotiation of reinsurance contracts.
Monitor investment performance and report investment performance to the Investment Committee of the Board of Directors.

Organizational & People Leadership:
Establish and maintain an effective organizational structure that supports the strategic delivery of services, ensuring alignment with corporate priorities and operational excellence.
Foster a unified and high-performing leadership team that is collaborative, future-focused, and committed to advancing the Corporation’s mission through continuous service improvement and innovation.
Champion a culture of accountability, inclusion, and excellence, where diverse perspectives are valued, calculated risks are embraced, and employees are empowered to deliver exceptional service and contribute meaningfully to the Corporation’s success.

Qualifications

Education:
Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries (FCIA) and Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS).
The CFA designation and/or strong investment knowledge is considered as an asset.

Experience:
Ten (10) years of senior leadership experience at the Director or Senior Director level, including five (5) years in a senior actuarial leadership capacity within the property and casualty insurance industry, with accountability for strategic rate setting, reserving, enterprise risk management, and actuarial governance.

Technical Knowledge and Skills:
Exceptional leadership skills with a proven ability to form, lead and develop high performing teams, and demonstrate successes in leading change.
Superior negotiation skills along with excellent interpersonal skills and proven success in public speaking and formal presentations.
Proven experience effectively and critically assessing different product and coverage scenarios and determining creative solutions that meet customers’ needs while demonstrating clear understanding of root cause, impacts and consequences of decisions on both customers and the corporation.
Strong organizational skills along with the ability to plan and manage multiple complex projects and tasks simultaneously will contribute to success in this role.
Capable of positively engaging executive management, the Board of Directors as well as influential external stakeholders (e.g. Government of Manitoba, strategic business partners, interest groups with diverging interests) and operate with the highest level of integrity and business ethics.

Head of Revenue - Full-time, Remote

Application Deadline: November 29th, 2026 @ 11:59pm EST

Build the revenue engine that takes BeMo to the next stage of growth.

Why BeMo?

At BeMo, our mission is rooted in the belief that education is a universal right, not a privilege. We help students pursue highly competitive professional programs through admissions consulting, test preparation, and technology-enabled services. Our team is remote, fast-moving, data-driven, and focused on measurable student and business outcomes.

The Role:

We are looking for a commercially rigorous Head of Revenue to own the full revenue system across demand generation, sales, expansion, lifecycle revenue, and revenue operations. This is not a traditional sales-leadership role. Your job is to identify the biggest constraint on profitable growth, quantify the opportunity, prioritize the highest-leverage initiatives, and lead cross-functional execution.

You will be accountable for increasing cash and revenue while protecting the quality and economics of growth. You will work directly with the CEO and lead the revenue organization toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory.

What You Will Own:

Company-wide revenue growth across marketing, sales, direct/self-serve revenue, upsells, cross-sells, downsells, saves, referrals, and reactivation.
Demand generation economics, including qualified lead volume, cost per qualified request, CAC, ROI/ROAS, and channel-level growth efficiency.
Sales performance, including completed consultations, revenue per completed call, conversion rate, AOV, show efficiency, response speed, and forecasting accuracy.
Pricing, packaging, offers, promotions, and lifecycle monetization designed to increase customer value without relying on short-term pull-forward tactics.
Revenue operations: attribution, dashboards, lead tracking, funnel measurement, forecasting, QA, and reliable experiment measurement.
A disciplined testing program across acquisition, landing pages, sales, follow-up, email/SMS/direct mail, offers, and expansion revenue.
Cross-functional prioritization: decide where the next dollar and the next hour of team capacity create the highest expected incremental value.
Revenue leadership systems that reduce dependence on any single individual and create repeatable, scalable execution.

How Success Will Be Measured:

The role carries a significant performance-based component aligned with the same outcomes the role controls. Performance is evaluated across three dimensions:
Cash growth: durable improvement in actual cash received.
Demand generation: growth in qualified demand and channel economics, not traffic or lead volume in isolation.
Strategic execution: completion and quality of the systems, experiments, reporting, automation, and longer-term initiatives required to compound revenue growth.

These outcomes are also subject to a company growth-driver score that prevents one strong metric from masking deterioration elsewhere in the revenue system. The objective is sustainable progress toward BeMo's long-term growth trajectory, not local optimization of one department.

What You Will Do:

Diagnose the revenue funnel and identify the highest-value constraint before prescribing solutions.
Build quarterly revenue plans with quantified assumptions, targets, owners, timelines, and expected impact.
Lead the Sales Manager and coordinate tightly with marketing, operations, support, finance, and DevOps.
Set and monitor leading and lagging KPIs across acquisition, sales, and expansion revenue.
Design and review experiments with defined hypotheses, controls, success metrics, guardrails, and decision rules.
Improve the economics of paid and organic acquisition while maintaining sufficient qualified demand for the sales organization.
Increase revenue per lead and revenue per customer through better conversion, AOV, offers, upsells, cross-sells, and reactivation.
Build accurate forecasting, attribution, and executive reporting so decisions are based on trusted data.
Use AI and automation where they improve speed, conversion, decision quality, or operating leverage.
Develop leaders, delegate execution appropriately, and hold teams accountable for both results and quality.

We’d Love to Hear From You if You…

Have 7+ years of progressively senior revenue, growth, commercial, sales, or marketing leadership experience.
Can demonstrate material revenue growth you personally helped cause, with baseline, endpoint, time period, and measurable contribution.
Have owned more than one part of the revenue system - ideally demand generation plus sales, lifecycle/expansion, or RevOps.
Are highly quantitative and can translate funnel changes into incremental revenue, cash, CAC, and contribution economics.
Have managed leaders and teams rather than relying on personal heroics.
Can distinguish correlation from causation and are comfortable changing your view when the data contradicts your initial hypothesis.
Know how to prioritize aggressively and can explain what should not be done yet.
Have strong attention to detail, forecasting discipline, and operating cadence.
Are comfortable in a remote, high-accountability environment and can work across functions without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Compensation & Location:

Remote role. Potential total annual compensation up to $300,000+ CAD, including competitive base compensation and a significant performance based bonus tied to cash growth, demand generation, strategic execution, and progress against the company's long term revenue growth plan. Final compensation will depend on experience and performance.

Our Hiring Process:

Our hiring process includes multiple steps. You will progress to each step if we believe there's a good match for both parties. The process includes a review of your application, a skills assessment test, a virtual OR phone interview, a face-to-face interview with select members of our team via video conference and lastly, reference calls.

How to Apply:

Simple. Click "Apply" and fill out the short application form.

We won’t be able to individually respond to all applicants, but if we feel that you’re a strong match, we will be in touch via email to proceed with your application. Thanks, and we look forward to hearing from you!

Turn feedback across accounts into roadmap priorities, scope fixes for adoption blockers with Engineering, and tell customers what we built for them

You build a process, then run it yourself until someone else can.

You use AI tools every day to work faster and better, and you can show us how. This is required for every role at SiftMed.

Experience with Salesforce or product analytics tools

Within 3 months: Run your first pilot and onboard new customers using a playbook you've written

new_jobs.title: Director of FP&A
new_jobs.description:
Senior FP&A leadership opportunity with a large, well-established North American manufacturing and distribution company headquartered in Vancouver. Excellent opportunity for an experienced finance leader who enjoys combining strategic financial oversight with hands-on analysis, developing high-performing teams, and influencing executive-level decision-making. Competitive compensation, excellent benefits, and a collaborative corporate culture.

Who- the Company:

Our client is a very well-established and successful manufacturing and distribution company with operations across North America, 2000 employees, 10+ legal entities, 30+ operating sites across Canada and the US, etc. They have a great reputation among their happy customers and partners. The 40+ person finance team is collaborative and friendly, and the leaders promote productive workdays with plenty of communication and organization to limit unnecessary overtime.

The company is recognized for its commitment to operational excellence, continuous improvement, and professional development. Its finance team works collaboratively with senior leadership and business stakeholders to support organizational performance and long-term growth.

What- the Role:

Our client seeking a new Director of Financial Planning & Analysis
to lead its enterprise-wide FP&A function. Reporting to the Vice President of Strategy, this is a hands-on leadership position responsible for overseeing financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and analysis across a large and complex North American organization.
The Director will lead and develop the FP&A team while partnering closely with the VP, CFO, executive leadership, Finance Business Partners, and other cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen financial planning discipline, improve forecasting accuracy, and deliver meaningful financial insights that support business decisions.

Key Responsibilities include:

Budgeting & Forecasting:
Lead enterprise-wide budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning, including cash flow forecasting.
Financial Analysis & Reporting:
Oversee financial consolidation, performance analysis, and executive and Board reporting, identifying key business drivers, risks, and opportunities.
Financial Modelling & Capital Planning:
Lead scenario analysis, capital investment evaluations, and business case development to support strategic decision-making.
Business Partnership:
Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate performance, challenge assumptions, and provide actionable financial insights.
Process Improvement & Team Leadership:
Enhance FP&A processes, reporting standards, and forecasting accuracy while leading and developing a high-performing team.

SWIM will provide interested candidates with a detailed job description.

Who- the Candidate:

We are seeking a well-rounded senior-level FP&A professional with at least 10-15 years’ of progressive work experience, including around 5 years in people management. Canadian CPA designation and/or CFE will be viewed very favourably, as would MBA-Finance from a reputable University.
Qualified candidates will bring extensive experience leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, and management reporting functions, ideally within a large, complex, multi-site organization operating across Canada and the United States, and/or globally… i.e. $500M+ in revenues, 1000+ employees, and/or operations across multiple countries.
Experience within manufacturing, distribution, or other inventory-intensive industries
would be particularly relevant, given the organization's operational scale and complexity.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

Proven experience leading enterprise-wide budgeting and forecasting processes, including cash flow forecasting, and improving financial planning accuracy and discipline.
Strong financial modelling capabilities, including long-range planning, scenario analysis, capital investment evaluations, and business case development.
Experience consolidating financial information across multiple business units, regions, and operating entities.
Confidence presenting financial insights and recommendations to senior executives and influencing strategic business decisions.
A demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and develop finance professionals while remaining comfortable working hands-on with complex financial analysis.
Strong proficiency with financial systems, including SAP or comparable ERP platforms, and enterprise planning, reporting, and performance management tools. Experience with OneStream, Tableau, or similar platforms is an asset.
Beyond technical expertise, the ideal candidate is analytical and a collaborative leader, with strong business acumen
who can balance enterprise-level strategic thinking with attention to financial detail. Strong communication, business judgment, critical thinking, and the ability to constructively challenge assumptions are essential.
We are seeking someone who can build credibility with senior stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, drive continuous improvement, and develop a strong, accountable FP&A team.

How Much:

Competitive base salary commensurate with level of skills, experience, and education, likely in the range of $170,000 to $190,000, possibly with some upwards flexibility for highly qualified candidates who have many/most of the “nice to haves.” The company will provide their new Director of FP&A with a solid overall compensation package, including a generous variable compensation program, professional development support, and excellent health, dental, & vision benefits.

Where:

Corporate office in the heart of downtown Vancouver, working from office 4-5 days/week to allow for plenty of in-person relationship building, presentations/meetings, and collaboration. It is anticipated that there will be around 5% business travel in this role (within Canada and US).

If you already have a Recruiter at SWIM, please reach out to them directly. If you do not yet have a contact at SWIM Recruiting, please click ‘APPLY’
to submit your resume.
We thank all interested candidates for their consideration!
